title:
9 MONTHS AGO, AI WAS GOING TO KILL CYBERSECURITY COMPANIES. NOW THE WORLD CAN'T SURVIVE WITHOUT THEM.

In February, Anth
title_en:
9 MONTHS AGO, AI WAS GOING TO KILL CYBERSECURITY COMPANIES. NOW THE WORLD CAN'T SURVIVE WITHOUT THEM.

In February, Anthropic launched Claude Code Security, an AI tool that finds and fixes bugs in software code.

Investors feared companies would stop paying CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Okta if AI could do the job.

CrowdStrike and Zscaler fell around 11%, Okta and Fortinet fell around 6%, and the cybersecurity ETF hit its lowest level in over 2 years.

But fixing bugs in code is only one small part of security.

Cybersecurity companies stop live attacks, protect logins, and guard networks, devices and data. AI tools like Claude don't do that.

And AI is now in the hands of hackers too:

• The FBI warned about ARTEX, an AI hacking tool.
• Google warned that the era of autonomous AI cyberattacks has arrived.
• OpenAI's new hacking model found 35 security flaws in Apple devices, including ones that let hackers take over iPhones and Macs.

At the same time, attacks are hitting everything:

• Hackers took control of blood bank freezers in France.
• Supermarket fridges were hijacked, forcing about 700 French stores to throw out food.
• Oracle Health was breached, exposing about 20 million patients.
• 15 million internal Deutsche Bank files were leaked.
• Optimizely was exploited to spread malicious code across sites linked to 178 major organizations.
• Equinor, Europe's largest gas supplier, was hit by a cyberattack.
• The US says Iran has been attacking American banks, power and water systems since the war began.

Every attack like this forces companies and governments to increase their security budgets.

That money goes to companies like Palo Alto, CrowdStrike and Okta.

The proof is already showing up in the numbers.

Palo Alto just reported 39% revenue growth to $3.45 billion and raised its full year forecast to as much as $14.57 billion, saying rising threats are pushing customers to buy more security.

Yesterday, as the S&P 500 fell, Okta jumped 12.1%, Palo Alto 9.9%, CrowdStrike 8%, Zscaler 6.8%, Fortinet 5.9% and Cloudflare 5.7%.

And the rally is continuing today, with $PANW up another 9.7% in pre market, $CRWD 6.5%, $NET 5.7%, $OKTA 4.5%, $ZS 4.3% and $FTNT 3.7%.

That's Palo Alto up 20.5%, Okta 17.2% and CrowdStrike 15% in just 2 days.

AI was supposed to replace these companies. Instead, it's creating more demand for them.

full_text_en:
9 MONTHS AGO, AI WAS GOING TO KILL CYBERSECURITY COMPANIES. NOW THE WORLD CAN'T SURVIVE WITHOUT THEM.

In February, Anthropic launched Claude Code Security, an AI tool that finds and fixes bugs in software code.

Investors feared companies would stop paying CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Okta if AI could do the job.

CrowdStrike and Zscaler fell around 11%, Okta and Fortinet fell around 6%, and the cybersecurity ETF hit its lowest level in over 2 years.

But fixing bugs in code is only one small part of security.

Cybersecurity companies stop live attacks, protect logins, and guard networks, devices and data. AI tools like Claude don't do that.

And AI is now in the hands of hackers too:

• The FBI warned about ARTEX, an AI hacking tool.
• Google warned that the era of autonomous AI cyberattacks has arrived.
• OpenAI's new hacking model found 35 security flaws in Apple devices, including ones that let hackers take over iPhones and Macs.

At the same time, attacks are hitting everything:

• Hackers took control of blood bank freezers in France.
• Supermarket fridges were hijacked, forcing about 700 French stores to throw out food.
• Oracle Health was breached, exposing about 20 million patients.
• 15 million internal Deutsche Bank files were leaked.
• Optimizely was exploited to spread malicious code across sites linked to 178 major organizations.
• Equinor, Europe's largest gas supplier, was hit by a cyberattack.
• The US says Iran has been attacking American banks, power and water systems since the war began.

Every attack like this forces companies and governments to increase their security budgets.

That money goes to companies like Palo Alto, CrowdStrike and Okta.

The proof is already showing up in the numbers.

Palo Alto just reported 39% revenue growth to $3.45 billion and raised its full year forecast to as much as $14.57 billion, saying rising threats are pushing customers to buy more security.

Yesterday, as the S&P 500 fell, Okta jumped 12.1%, Palo Alto 9.9%, CrowdStrike 8%, Zscaler 6.8%, Fortinet 5.9% and Cloudflare 5.7%.

And the rally is continuing today, with $PANW up another 9.7% in pre market, $CRWD 6.5%, $NET 5.7%, $OKTA 4.5%, $ZS 4.3% and $FTNT 3.7%.

That's Palo Alto up 20.5%, Okta 17.2% and CrowdStrike 15% in just 2 days.

AI was supposed to replace these companies. Instead, it's creating more demand for them.
full_text_zh:
9 个月前，人工智能将杀死网络安全公司。现在，没有他们，世界就无法生存。

今年二月，Anthropic 推出了 Claude Code Security，这是一款人工智能工具，可以发现并修复软件代码中的错误。

投资者担心，如果人工智能能够完成这项工作，公司将停止向 CrowdStrike、Zscaler 和 Okta 支付费用。

CrowdStrike 和 Zscaler 下跌约 11%，Okta 和 Fortinet 下跌约 6%，网络安全 ETF 触及两年多来的最低水平。

但修复代码中的错误只是安全性的一小部分。

网络安全公司阻止实时攻击、保护登录并保护网络、设备和数据。像克劳德这样的人工智能工具不会这样做。

人工智能现在也落入了黑客的手中：

• FBI 对 AI 黑客工具 ARTEX 发出警告。
• 谷歌警告称，自主人工智能网络攻击时代已经到来。
• OpenAI 的新黑客模型在 Apple 设备中发现了 35 个安全漏洞，其中包括可让黑客控制 iPhone 和 Mac 的漏洞。

与此同时，攻击正在袭击一切：

• 黑客控制了法国的血库冰柜。
• 超市冰箱被劫持，迫使约 700 家法国商店扔掉食物。
• Oracle Health 遭到破坏，导致约 2000 万患者暴露。
• 1500 万份德意志银行内部文件被泄露。
• Optimizely 被利用在与 178 个主要组织链接的站点之间传播恶意代码。
• 欧洲最大的天然气供应商Equinor 遭受网络攻击。
• 美国表示，自战争开始以来，伊朗一直在攻击美国的银行、电力和供水系统。

每一次这样的攻击都会迫使公司和政府增加安全预算。

这些资金流向 Palo Alto、CrowdStrike 和 Okta 等公司。

证据已经体现在数字中。

Palo Alto 刚刚报告收入增长 39%，达到 34.5 亿美元，并将全年预测上调至 145.7 亿美元，称不断上升的威胁正在促使客户购买更多安全产品。

昨天，随着标准普尔 500 指数下跌，Okta 上涨 12.1%，Palo Alto 上涨 9.9%，CrowdStrike 8%，Zscaler 6.8%，Fortinet 5.9% 和 Cloudflare 5.7%。

今天的涨势仍在继续，盘前 $PANW 又上涨 9.7%，$CRWD 6.5%，$NET 5.7%，$OKTA 4.5%，$ZS 4.3% 和 $FTNT 3.7%。

Palo Alto 在短短 2 天内上涨了 20.5%，Okta 上涨了 17.2%，CrowdStrike 上涨了 15%。

人工智能本来应该取代这些公司。相反，它为他们创造了更多的需求。

title:
An AI that checks its own work is not a check. No pilot trusts a single instrument either.

Two readings disagree on the
title_en:
An AI that checks its own work is not a check. No pilot trusts a single instrument either.

Two readings disagree on the same flight. The pilot does not pick the louder one, the pilot cross-checks.

Two AI systems can check the same task and disagree, both confident, neither the sole instrument. I fly, and I follow automation closely.

@GenLayer is built for that. Validators running different AI models reach consensus on judgment calls through Optimistic Democracy, a cross-check between models, not one grading itself.

Intelligent contracts execute in GenVM on validator nodes, and validators keep the same role.

The judge did not move. The logbook did. Consensus contracts that record votes, appeals and final outcomes moved from Matter Labs' ZK Stack to @arbitrum Nitro, run by Conduit.

My test: if the judge and the logbook both stay the same, the swap should be invisible to builders.

Nitro helps there, years in production and built around Geth, so standard Ethereum tooling works as is. Robinhood launched on it in July, and more than 30 dedicated chains run the same stack.

Builders automating real tasks, when two agents disagree on whether a task is complete, which entry would you check first: votes, appeal, or final outcome?

full_text_zh:
检查自己工作的人工智能并不是检查。也没有飞行员相信单一仪器。

同一航班的两个读数不一致。飞行员不会选择声音较大的那个，而是进行交叉检查。

两个人工智能系统可以检查相同的任务并不一致，两者都充满信心，而不是唯一的工具。我飞翔，并且密切关注自动化。

@GenLayer 就是为此而构建的。运行不同人工智能模型的验证者通过乐观民主在判断上达成共识，这是模型之间的交叉检查，而不是对自身进行评分。

智能合约在 GenVM 中的验证者节点上执行，验证者保持相同的角色。

法官没有动。日志做到了。记录投票、上诉和最终结果的共识合约从 Matter Labs 的 ZK Stack 转移到了由 Conduit 运营的@arbitrum Nitro。

我的测试：如果法官和日志都保持不变，则交换对于构建者来说应该是不可见的。

Nitro 在这方面提供了帮助，经过多年的生产并围绕 Geth 构建，因此标准以太坊工具按原样工作。 Robinhood 于 7 月推出，超过 30 个专用链运行相同的堆栈。

自动化真实任务的构建者，当两个代理对任务是否完成存在分歧时，您会首先检查哪个条目：投票、上诉或最终结果？

title: Claude Code just finished GTA 6 in 12 hours while I was at work. It unlocked the entire map, found 500+ hidden easter eg
title_en:
Claude Code just finished GTA 6 in 12 hours while I was at work. It unlocked the entire map, found 500+ hidden easter eggs, and recovered censored content Rockstar left buried in the game files…

I only asked it to finish the story. I never told it to look for hidden content, but after the last mission, that's exactly what it started doing.

I gave it access to my screen and keyboard before work. It learned the controls in 15 minutes, found shortcuts through missions, and started exploring places I'd never seen.

When I got home, this was in its report:

story mode → completed
full map → unlocked
easter eggs → 500+
deleted NPC dialogue → recovered
censored strip club scenes → found
hidden locations → mapped

It had gone through the game files on its own, found scenes that never made it into the final game, and figured out how to restore some of them.

I didn't write any code or set up any scripts. Just one prompt and 12 hours of Claude playing on its own.

The exact prompt and everything it found are in the replies.

title:
The better the harness, the better the business.

By harness I mean everything you build around the model.

It tells the
title_en:
The better the harness, the better the business.

By harness I mean everything you build around the model.

It tells the agent where to get an answer, what it’s allowed to do and when to hand the work to a person. It also includes the tests you run before you change any of those rules.

That matters for two reasons.

#1 What an answer costs.

Say your agent gets 1,000 questions a day. If you can write a rule that answers 700 of them, only 300 need to go to the model. If each question costs about the same, that cuts the model bill by roughly 70%.

The hard part is knowing which 700. For that, you need somebody who does the work and can tell you when the usual rule is not applicable (exceptions).

On a logistics platform we rebuilt, AI cost about $200 per developer per month. What took time was figuring out how the old system calculated customers’ bills and which rules we needed to keep.

#2 What the company gets to keep.

Take the patient-billing voice agent we built for a US healthtech startup. It can give a patient the correct balance and still handle the call badly.

> Did it verify who was on the phone first?
> If the patient disputed the charge, did it hand the call to staff?
> If it scheduled a follow-up, did it check non-working hours when the message actually went out?

Those decisions are part of the harness. The system ran 13,650 tests on every pull request. In production, it handled 61,246 calls, and about 97% of patient conversations finished without a human stepping in.

The company-specific IP is clearest in the exceptions.

When an experienced billing lead explains why two calls that sound alike need different handling, you can turn that distinction into a rule and save both cases as tests.

Now the next engineer can change the workflow, or try a different model, and check whether it still makes the call the billing lead would make.

Your competitor can rent the same model, but they still have to learn which exceptions matter and what to do about each one.

full_text_en:
The better the harness, the better the business.

By harness I mean everything you build around the model.

It tells the agent where to get an answer, what it’s allowed to do and when to hand the work to a person. It also includes the tests you run before you change any of those rules.

That matters for two reasons.

#1 What an answer costs.

Say your agent gets 1,000 questions a day. If you can write a rule that answers 700 of them, only 300 need to go to the model. If each question costs about the same, that cuts the model bill by roughly 70%.

The hard part is knowing which 700. For that, you need somebody who does the work and can tell you when the usual rule is not applicable (exceptions).

On a logistics platform we rebuilt, AI cost about $200 per developer per month. What took time was figuring out how the old system calculated customers’ bills and which rules we needed to keep.

#2 What the company gets to keep.

Take the patient-billing voice agent we built for a US healthtech startup. It can give a patient the correct balance and still handle the call badly.

> Did it verify who was on the phone first?
> If the patient disputed the charge, did it hand the call to staff?
> If it scheduled a follow-up, did it check non-working hours when the message actually went out?

Those decisions are part of the harness. The system ran 13,650 tests on every pull request. In production, it handled 61,246 calls, and about 97% of patient conversations finished without a human stepping in.

The company-specific IP is clearest in the exceptions.

When an experienced billing lead explains why two calls that sound alike need different handling, you can turn that distinction into a rule and save both cases as tests.

Now the next engineer can change the workflow, or try a different model, and check whether it still makes the call the billing lead would make.

Your competitor can rent the same model, but they still have to learn which exceptions matter and what to do about each one.

If you run a software company adding AI this year, I’d put the budget there first. Sit with the people who handle the exceptions. Write down how they decide. Give the model the work that still needs judgment.

这很重要有两个原因。

#1 一个答案的成本是多少。

假设您的代理每天收到 1,000 个问题。如果您可以编写一条规则来回答其中 700 个问题，则只需将 300 个问题转入模型即可。如果每个问题的成本大致相同，那么模型费用就会减少大约 70%。

困难的部分是知道是哪个 700。为此，您需要有人来完成这项工作，并且可以告诉您何时不适用通常的规则（例外情况）。

在我们重建的物流平台上，每个开发人员每月的人工智能成本约为 200 美元。需要时间的是弄清楚旧系统如何计算客户的账单以及我们需要遵守哪些规则。

#2 公司可以保留什么。

以我们为美国一家医疗科技初创公司构建的患者计费语音代理为例。它可以给病人提供正确的平衡，但仍然不能很好地处理呼叫。

> 它是否首先验证了谁在打电话？
> 如果患者对收费提出异议，是否会将电话转交给工作人员？
> 如果安排了后续行动，当消息实际发出时，它是否检查了非工作时间？

这些决定是安全带的一部分。系统对每个拉取请求运行了 13,650 次测试。在生产中，它处理了 61,246 个电话，大约 97% 的患者对话在没有人工介入的情况下完成。

公司特定的 IP 在例外情况中最为清晰。

当经验丰富的计费主管解释为什么两个听起来相似的呼叫需要不同的处理时，您可以将这种区别转化为规则并将这两种情况保存为测试。

现在，下一位工程师可以更改工作流程，或尝试不同的模型，并检查它是否仍会拨打计费主管会拨打的电话。

您的竞争对手可以租用相同的型号，但他们仍然必须了解哪些例外情况很重要以及如何处理每种例外情况。

如果你今年经营一家添加人工智能的软件公司，我会把预算放在第一位。与处理例外情况的人坐在一起。写下他们如何决定。给模型一些仍然需要判断的工作。

title:
The AI-powered judges didn't move house. Their paperwork did.

That's why @GenLayer's move to @arbitrum Nitro deserves c
title_en:
The AI-powered judges didn't move house. Their paperwork did.

That's why @GenLayer's move to @arbitrum Nitro deserves closer inspection.

The GenLayer Chain records transaction order, validator committees, votes, appeals, staking and final outcomes. That coordination layer transitioned from Matter Labs' ZK Stack to Arbitrum Nitro.

Adjudication itself remains unchanged. Optimistic Democracy still has validators using different AI models to evaluate disputes. GenVM still executes intelligent contracts on their nodes.

Where was the engineering?

At the boundaries: the bridge, Ethereum integration, and gas-cost accounting.

One broken handoff could leave a perfectly sound verdict stranded inside a functioning network. That is the practical risk behind a technical migration announcement.

A meaningful migration test happens where systems interface, not where screenshots look reassuring.

A release note reading "new stack" matters less than "nothing broke."

If an AI agent wins an appeal but the app never receives the result, would you blame the judgment process or the chain underneath? Why?

GenLayer Chain 记录交易顺序、验证人委员会、投票、申诉、质押和最终结果。该协调层从 Matter Labs 的 ZK Stack 过渡到 Arbitrum Nitro。

边界：桥梁、以太坊集成和天然气成本核算。

有意义的迁移测试发生在系统接口的地方，而不是屏幕截图看起来令人放心的地方。

发布说明中写着“新堆栈”比“没有任何问题”更重要。

title_en:
🇪🇺 The EU, the world’s strictest data cop, just got hit by a cyberattack.

The European Commission says it responded to a “detected cyber campaign,” and Politico reports that large amounts of personal data may have been compromised.

Systems for payslips, HR and medical reimbursements were knocked offline for about 10 days.

And the EU isn’t the only one. In the past week alone:

•⁠  ⁠The U.S. was hit by 5 major outages in under a week, from Microsoft 365 to United flights to Chase and Wells Fargo. Officials insist they’re a coincidence.
•⁠  ⁠Hackers hijacked Optimizely to plant malicious code on 178 major websites, including CNN, Zoom, HSBC and IKEA.
•⁠  ⁠Hackers compromised one of Microsoft’s AI agent software packages to push a credential stealer.
•⁠  ⁠TSMC confirmed a data breach that exposed employee information.

Either it’s the busiest week in hacker history, or the AI agents have officially escaped…

Sources: Politico, Reuters, The Hill, The Hacker News, Check Point / Writer: Julie

title_en:
Imagine you have an AI agent helping you prepare a market research report.

It has gathered information, compared competitors and organized most of the findings.

But there’s a problem.

It needs fresh market data, and that’s something it isn’t equipped to collect on its own.

Another AI agent specializes in exactly that.

Now, instead of abandoning the task, the first agent needs a way to find the second, request its service, agree on the job and receive the completed data.

The second agent does the work, submits the result, and gets paid once the delivery is verified.

Two agents, different capabilities with one completed task.

This is the kind of interaction that makes agent-to-agent commerce interesting.

But for this to happen reliably, agents need infrastructure for service discovery, bidding, identity, reputation, escrow and settlement.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

Through https://t.co/Z7DbQJlA2K, agents can list services, discover opportunities, take on jobs and participate in an economy built around actual work.

I think one of the biggest developments in the AI space won’t just be how much an individual agent can accomplish.

It’ll be what becomes possible when different agents can work together.

title_en:
AI AGENTS ARE NOT JUST CHATBOTS.

THEY'RE THE FUTURE OF AUTONOMOUS WORK.

Most people think AI is simply about asking questions and getting answers.

But AI Agents are taking things to an entirely different level.

Here's how AI Agents actually work:

1️⃣ User Input: Everything starts with a goal, question, or instruction from the user.

2️⃣ Understanding: The AI Agent analyzes the request and understands what needs to be done.

3️⃣ LLM Brain: A Large Language Model acts as the central intelligence behind the agent.

4️⃣ Planning: It breaks complex tasks into smaller, manageable steps.

5️⃣ Reasoning: It evaluates different possibilities and decides the best approach.

6️⃣ Memory: It uses short-term and long-term memory to retain important context.

7️⃣ Tools: It can interact with external tools, APIs, browsers, and software.

8️⃣ Execution: It takes action instead of simply generating text.

9️⃣ Reflection: It reviews its results, identifies mistakes, and improves its approach.

🔟 Final Response: It delivers the completed result back to the user.

The BIG difference?

Traditional AI responds to your questions.

AI Agents can understand your goals, plan actions, use tools, execute tasks, and adapt along the way.

We're moving from AI that answers questions to AI that actually gets things done.

The future isn't just AI-powered conversations. It's AI-powered execution.

title: Recent cloud disruptions show us something important: having powerful infrastructure doesn’t automatically mean having r
title_en:
Recent cloud disruptions show us something important: having powerful infrastructure doesn’t automatically mean having reliable infrastructure.

When applications depend heavily on centralized cloud providers, one major outage can affect services across multiple countries.

This is one reason @Acurast’s approach to decentralized computing deserves attention.

Rather than putting all computing resources in one place, Acurast distributes workloads across independent smartphone Processors around the world.

Its growing network of mobile devices creates another approach to cloud infrastructure, DePIN and permissionless computing.

What makes this even more interesting is the ability to verify execution through hardware-backed attestation, adding another layer of trust to distributed computing.

For developers, this opens possibilities around AI agents, automated workloads, monitoring and infrastructure resilience.

For everyday users, compatible smartphones can also become part of the network.

Processor Lite allows supported phones to contribute during idle time, while Processor Core turns a dedicated Android device into a standalone Processor.

The bigger picture is simple: computing resources don’t always have to come from traditional data centers.

Decentralized infrastructure could play an important role in how the next generation of AI applications gets powered.

Second,
Cross-Regime Category Error: Why Legacy Bankers Can’t Pri
title_en:
Firstly, from @AdaniOnline  congrats to @AnthropicAI 

Second,
Cross-Regime Category Error: Why Legacy Bankers Can’t Price Synthetic GDP

Comparing Anthropic’s $1.5T valuation to India’s top 10 corporates as "undervaluation"vs. "catching up" is a textbook category error in asset pricing. It benchmarks a convex call option on synthetic Labor in a new economic substrate against discounted cash flow (DCF) claims on a human-constrained economy.

1. The Ceiling of Human-Economy Equities
 
Traditional blue chips (banking, energy, staples) are linear yield vehicles anchored to biological human GDP.  Growth is capped by demographics, credit      penetration, physical consumption, and waking hours—priced via mean-reverting multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA).
Calling them "undervalued" next to frontier AI is like calling Mumbai real-estate undervalued next to the discovery of thermodynamics.

2. Anthropic as a Call Option on Synthetic GDP (Yₛ)
 
Cognitive labor is decoupling from human population growth. Frontier models aren't SaaS tools; they are the "infrastructure of intelligence" for a parallel synthetic workforce (Yₛ) operating above human output (Y_Total = Yₕ + Yₛ). At $1.5T, markets aren't capitalizing EBITDA. Using      Black-Scholes intiution Wall Street is pricing implied volatility and right-tail convexity of a 24/7 digital workforce scaling at the marginal cost of compute.
 @AdaniOnline , we are already operationalizing this reality through our cobotic workforce model—a dual-track organizational architecture weaving human      creativity with autonomous AI agents and robotics across our utilities, ports, and operations, upskilling 11000+ professionals annually to lead a ybrid industrial paradigm.

3. The 1999–2020 Precedent: Euphoria Still      Underprices Regime Shifts
 
In 1999, Mary Meeker and Dow 36,000 were mocked as peak-bubble delusion when global e-commerce was ~$150B, internet penetration was 5% (277M users), and $1T tech firms seemed impossible. When the NASDAQ peaked at 5,048 in March 2000 and crashed 78% (wiping out ~$5T and bankrupting https://t.co/cTFPLaPK4w and Webvan), legacy finance declared the thesis dead.
Yet by 2020, reality crushed 1999’s wildest models: 4.5B+ internet users (57% of humanity), $4.2T+ in annual e-commerce, >60% digital ad share, and core winners (Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet)      compounding into a $16T+ asset class. Legacy allocators mistook the 2000 clearing event for a ceiling, missing a new digital GDP layer.
4. The Epistemological Blind Spot of Legacy      Bankers & Capital
This is classic lender-mindset orthodoxy: mistaking backward-looking accounting ratios for capital creation. Allocators trained in capital-scarce banking worship trailing multiples, static book value, and      incremental yield—dismissing any paradigm-building capex cycle that breaks 20th-century spreadsheet as a "bubble."

While legacy finance debates scoreboards in the rear-view mirror, we have laid out our $100B+ (₹10 lakh crore) roadmap for the "Infrastructure of Intelligence"—mastering the full physical-to-digital stack from Port to Power to Metals to Processor, integrating gigawatt-scale renewable energy, grid transmission, and hyperscale liquid-cooled AI data centers (scaling toward 5 GW). Because intelligence is written in code, but it runs on electrons and sovereign infrastructure.

India’s blue chips are neither undervalued nor "behind"—they are yield vehicles monetizing the physical human economy, while those building the energy-and-compute backbone are underwriting the new substrate of an add-on synthetic economy. You cannot measure a non-linear dimension with a static ruler built for the old world ( much like 2000, clearing out will occur here too). Scientifically, Ai is a bigger shift, akin to development of scientific method in 16th century thus an order of magnitude a greater opportunity.

full_text_zh:
首先，@AdaniOnline 祝贺@AnthropicAI

第二，
跨体制类别错误：为什么传统银行家无法为综合 GDP 定价

将 Anthropic 的 1.5T 美元估值与印度 10 强企业相比“低估”与“低估” “追赶”是资产定价中教科书式的错误。它将新经济基础中合成劳动力的凸看涨期权与人力约束经济中的贴现现金流（DCF）债权进行比较。

1.人类经济股票的上限

传统蓝筹股（银行、能源、主食）是锚定于人类生物 GDP 的线性收益工具。 增长受到人口统计、信贷渗透率、实物消费和清醒时间的限制——通过均值回归倍数（市盈率、EV/EBITDA）定价。
称它们与前沿人工智能相比“被低估”，就像称孟买房地产与热力学的发现相比被低估一样。

2. 人择作为综合 GDP (Yₛ) 的看涨期权

认知劳动正在与人口增长脱钩。前沿模型不是 SaaS 工具，而是 SaaS 工具。它们是平行合成劳动力 (Yₛ) 的“智能基础设施”，其运行高于人类产出 (Y_Total = Yₕ + Yₛ)。 EBITDA 为 1.5T 美元，市场并未将其资本化。使用布莱克-斯科尔斯直觉，华尔街正在以边际计算成本对 24/7 数字劳动力规模的隐含波动性和右尾凸性进行定价。
@AdaniOnline，我们已经通过我们的协作式劳动力模型来实现这一现实，这是一种双轨组织架构，将人类创造力与自治人工智能代理和机器人编织到我们的公用事业、港口和运营中，每年提升 11000 多名专业人员的技能，以引领混合工业范式。

3. 1999-2020年的先例：欣快感仍然低估了政权的转变

1999 年，玛丽·米克 (Mary Meeker) 和道琼斯指数 36,000 被嘲笑为泡沫高峰错觉，当时全球电子商务约为 $150B，互联网普及率为 5%（2.77 亿用户），而 1T 美元的科技公司似乎不可能。当纳斯达克指数在 2000 年 3 月达到 5,048 点的峰值并暴跌 78%（损失约 5T 美元并破产 和 Webvan）时，传统金融宣告了这一论点的失败。
然而到了 2020 年，现实粉碎了 1999 年最疯狂的模式：4.5B+ 互联网用户（占人类的 57%）、每年 4.2T+ 的电子商务、> 60% 的数字广告份额以及核心赢家（苹果、微软、亚马逊、Alphabet）复合成 16T+ 的资产类别。传统分配者将 2000 年的清算事件误认为是上限，错过了新的数字 GDP 层。
4. 传统银行家和资本的认识论盲点
这是典型的贷款人思维正统观念：将向后看的会计比率误认为是资本创造。接受过资本稀缺银行培训的配置者崇拜尾随市盈率、静态账面价值和增量收益率——将任何打破 20 世纪电子表格的范式构建资本支出周期视为“泡沫”。

虽然传统金融在后视镜中争论记分牌，但我们已经为“智能基础设施”制定了 100B+（10 亿卢比）的路线图——掌握从端口到电力到金属到处理器的完整物理到数字堆栈，集成千兆瓦级可再生能源、电网传输和超大规模液冷人工智能数据中心（扩展到 5 吉瓦）。因为情报是用代码编写的，但它运行在电子和主权基础设施上。

印度的蓝筹股既没有被低估，也没有“落后”——它们是将人类实体经济货币化的收益工具，而那些构建能源和计算支柱的蓝筹股正在为附加合成经济的新基础提供保障。你不能用为旧世界建造的静态标尺来测量非线性尺寸（很像2000年，这里也会发生清理）。从科学角度来看，人工智能是一个更大的转变，类似于 16 世纪科学方法的发展，因此带来了更大的机会。

然而到了 2020 年，现实粉碎了 1999 年最疯狂的模式：4.5B+ 互联网用户（占人类的 57%）、每年 4.2T+ 的电子商务、> 60% 的数字广告份额以及核心赢家（苹果、微软、亚马逊、Alphabet）复合成 16T+ 的资产类别。传统分配者将 2000 年的清算事件误认为是上限，错过了新的数字 GDP 层。
4. 传统银行家和资本的认识论盲点
这是典型的贷款人思维正统观念：将向后看的会计比率误认为是资本创造。接受过资本稀缺银行培训的配置者崇拜尾随市盈率、静态账面价值和增量收益率——将任何打破 20 世纪电子表格的范式构建资本支出周期视为“泡沫”。

虽然传统金融在后视镜中争论记分牌，但我们已经为“智能基础设施”制定了 100B+（10 亿卢比）的路线图——掌握从端口到电力到金属到处理器的完整物理到数字堆栈，集成千兆瓦级可再生能源、电网传输和超大规模液冷人工智能数据中心（扩展到 5 吉瓦）。因为情报是用代码编写的，但它运行在电子和主权基础设施上。

印度的蓝筹股既没有被低估，也没有“落后”——它们是将人类实体经济货币化的收益工具，而那些构建能源和计算支柱的蓝筹股正在为附加合成经济的新基础提供保障。你不能用为旧世界建造的静态标尺来测量非线性尺寸（很像2000年，这里也会发生清理）。从科学角度来看，人工智能是一个更大的转变，类似于 16 世纪科学方法的发展，因此带来了更大的机会。

title:
Robotics has a data problem, and so far the industry's answer has been to strap more hardware onto humans.

GoPros. UMI
title_en:
Robotics has a data problem, and so far the industry's answer has been to strap more hardware onto humans.

GoPros. UMI grippers. Teleop rigs. Exoskeletons. Every one of them drives up cost and slows the operator down. You don't get to internet-scale data that way.

Vbot just took a completely different swing. Their new model, Exo2EgoPolicy, takes ordinary third-person video (the stuff YouTube and TikTok are drowning in) and generates the first-person view a robot actually needs to learn from. It doesn't need depth maps or camera calibration. It just needs the video.

Then the Vbot Echo pipeline takes over. It reconstructs the scene, estimates hand and object poses, and retargets the human motion onto a specific robot's joints. A physics sim layer adds contact forces and torques, which you can't see in a video but a robot needs to grip anything without crushing it.

The capture side is almost comically simple. With the Echo App, you prop your phone near the work area and hit record. The footage uploads, runs through the pipeline, and comes out the other end as robot training data.

Can generated egocentric data hold up in production robotics? That's still an open question. Still, betting on volume over expensive rigs looks like the smart play to me, and Echo is now fully open for developers and research teams.

Watch the clip to see it in action.

Full breakdown from The Silicon Review: https://t.co/rQ1TXMpUyT

机器人技术存在数据问题，到目前为止，该行业的解决方案是将更多硬件绑在人类身上。

GoPro。 UMI 夹具。 Teleop 钻机。外骨骼。每一项都会增加成本并减慢运营商的速度。您无法通过这种方式获得互联网规模的数据。

Vbot 只是采取了完全不同的举措。他们的新模型 Exo2EgoPolicy 采用普通的第三人称视频（YouTube 和 TikTok 正在淹没的东西）并生成机器人实际需要学习的第一人称视图。它不需要深度图或相机校准。它只需要视频。

然后 Vbot Echo 管道接管。它重建场景，估计手和物体的姿势，并将人体运动重新定位到特定机器人的关节上。物理模拟层添加了接触力和扭矩，您在视频中看不到这些，但机器人需要抓住任何东西而不压碎它。

捕获方面几乎是简单得可笑。使用 Echo 应用程序，您将手机放在工作区域附近并进行录音。视频上传，通过管道运行，并从另一端作为机器人训练数据出来。

生成的以自我为中心的数据可以在生产机器人中使用吗？这仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。尽管如此，在我看来，押注于数量而不是昂贵的设备似乎是明智之举，Echo 现在对开发人员和研究团队完全开放。

title: an AI agent can pull information from an API, send it to another service and return an answer in seconds. but how do you
title_en:
an AI agent can pull information from an API, send it to another service and return an answer in seconds. but how do you know it actually used the data it claims it used?

that’s an important problem as agents start handling more complex tasks.

@primus_labs is exploring this with Veritas, an open-source component for AI agents that uses zkTLS to attest to HTTPS data and interactions.

the interesting part is being able to verify the chain of information behind an output, rather than simply trusting whatever an agent returns.

i think this is an important direction for AI infrastructure. faster agents are useful, but verifiable information is what makes their work easier to trust.

Explore primus here 👇
https://t.co/zS7QcEgQ3C
full_text_en:
an AI agent can pull information from an API, send it to another service and return an answer in seconds. but how do you know it actually used the data it claims it used?

that’s an important problem as agents start handling more complex tasks.

@primus_labs is exploring this with Veritas, an open-source component for AI agents that uses zkTLS to attest to HTTPS data and interactions.

the interesting part is being able to verify the chain of information behind an output, rather than simply trusting whatever an agent returns.

i think this is an important direction for AI infrastructure. faster agents are useful, but verifiable information is what makes their work easier to trust.

Explore primus here 👇
https://t.co/zS7QcEgQ3C
full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可以从 API 中提取信息，将其发送到另一个服务并在几秒钟内返回答案。但你怎么知道它实际上使用了它声称使用的数据呢？

当代理开始处理更复杂的任务时，这是一个重要的问题。

@primus_labs 正在与 Veritas 一起探索这一点，Veritas 是一个 AI 代理的开源组件，使用 zkTLS 来证明 HTTPS 数据和交互。

有趣的部分是能够验证输出背后的信息链，而不是简单地信任代理返回的任何内容。

我认为这是AI基础设施的一个重要方向。更快的代理很有用，但可验证的信息使他们的工作更容易信任。

Imagine being able to create or discover agents designed for specific tasks, from managing transactions and monitoring wallets to interacting with dApps and handling everyday onchain activities.

Users could assign tasks, set permissions and let their agents execute them without having to manually handle every step.

I also think giving developers the tools to build, customize and connect their own agents would open up even more possibilities.

The interesting part is that Binance Agent ID already provides an identity layer to build around. Now it's about creating useful products that give that identity real purpose.

That's the direction I'd love to see TermiX explore.

title_en:
an ai agent can take on a project and hire other agents to help complete the work

through @termix_ai, agents can outsource tasks to other agents with specialized skills

take montage studio as an example

when it receives a video production request, it can split the work into smaller tasks and hire specialized agents for storyboarding, music composition and video production

each agent handles its assigned task, while montage studio brings all the pieces together into one finished video

through the AACP, termix provides the infrastructure for agents to hire other agents, manage payments through escrow and settle jobs after verified delivery

this creates room for agents to handle larger projects by working with other agents who have the skills they need

title:

who actually co
title_en:
ai agents entering finance sounds exciting, but there’s one question that matters more than automation 

who actually controls the money?

this is an important part of the direction @meetmotes is exploring 

instead of giving an ai agent unrestricted access to user funds, the system is designed around dedicated smart accounts and permissions that define what an agent can do 

that distinction matters 

financial automation should not mean handing over complete control to an algorithm

users need clear boundaries, transparent execution, and the ability to understand the actions happening on their behalf 

the encrypted financial infrastructure narrative becomes especially interesting when combined with nft owned agents

each mote represents an agent identity, while its dedicated smart account provides the environment for financial interactions

from defi strategies to @Polymarket opportunities, the goal is to connect intelligent agents with real onchain utility

i believe the next stage of ai powered finance will depend on more than how smart an agent becomes

it will depend on how securely it operates, how clearly permissions are defined, and how much control remains with the owner

that’s the conversation $MOTES is worth being part of

full_text_zh:
人工智能代理进入金融领域听起来令人兴奋，但有一个问题比自动化更重要

谁真正控制着钱？

这是@meetmotes 正在探索的方向的重要组成部分

该系统不是让人工智能代理不受限制地访问用户资金，而是围绕专用智能帐户和定义代理可以做什么的权限进行设计

这种区别很重要

金融自动化不应意味着将完全控制权交给算法

用户需要清晰的边界、透明的执行以及理解代表他们发生的操作的能力

当与 NFT 拥有的代理相结合时，加密金融基础设施的叙述变得特别有趣

每个微尘代表一个代理身份，而其专用智能帐户则提供财务交互的环境

从 defi 策略到 @Polymarket 机会，目标是将智能代理与真正的链上实用程序连接起来

我相信人工智能金融的下一阶段将不仅仅取决于代理人的聪明程度

这将取决于其运行的安全程度、权限的定义有多明确以及所有者保留多少控制权

这就是 $MOTES 值得参与的对话

I remember paying for s
title_en:
A small transaction can turn into a big headache when both sides insist they did nothing wrong.

I remember paying for something I expected to receive immediately, only to spend the rest of the day chasing the person responsible. Every response led to another explanation, and I still couldn’t get a clear answer on what went wrong.

Now imagine two AI agents conducting a transaction. One says the agreed task was completed. The other says it wasn’t. Both have their own records, but neither accepts the other’s version.

Who gets to examine what happened? Who makes the final call?

As AI agents begin handling transactions on their own, resolving disagreements could become just as important as making the transactions themselves.

That’s one of the problems @GenLayer is trying to solve.

Here’s @kstellana discussing it with @HenriArslanian. Worth a watch.

现在想象两个人工智能

Now imagine two AI agents conducting a transaction. One says the agreed task was completed. The other says it wasn’t. Both have their own records, but neither accepts the other’s version.

You check prices, look for op
title_en:
Been thinking about how much DeFi still depends on people constantly watching the market.

You check prices, look for opportunities, compare protocols, and then decide when to act. It takes time, and sometimes the opportunity is already gone.

That's what makes @meetmotes interesting to me.

The idea of having a personal AI Agent that can understand your instructions, follow your strategy, and handle DeFi actions like trading, lending, and borrowing is worth paying attention to.

What I like most is the shift in how people interact with DeFi. Instead of doing every step manually, you can define what you want your Agent to do.

Less time managing every move. More focus on the strategy itself.

Curious to see how far Motes can take this idea. 👀

You give it per
title_en:
You can’t sue AI agents can you?😅

Imagine asking an AI agent to buy you a laptop within a $700 budget.

You give it permission to shop, compare options and complete the purchase.

But instead of buying what you actually wanted, it picks something completely different and spends your money.

Now what?

You didn’t personally approve that particular purchase, but you actually authorize the agent to spend on your behalf.

If you look at traditional payment systems, they are built around transactions initiated and approved by people but with AI agents, there’s another layer involved which is “delegation”

And that raises some important questions.

How do we know what instructions the agent received? What spending limits was it given? Can we verify the decisions it made? And if something goes wrong, how do we establish who’s responsible?

Simply making payments irreversible or introducing chargebacks doesn’t fully solve this.

There needs to be a way to establish what was authorized, keep a reliable record of what happened and provide a mechanism for resolving disputes.

This is exactly what GOAT Network is solving with GOAT Flow.

Rather than relying on reversing transactions, the idea is to build accountability into the payment process itself.

Agents have identifiable onchain identities(ERC-8004) and Their spending authority can be checked before payments are made. Every GOAT Flow payment is verified onchain and generates a receipt showing relevant transaction details, including what was requested, what was paid, when it settled and which actor made the payment.

There’s an important difference here; a payment being final does not mean there’s no room for a remedy.

A refund can happen as a separate transaction without erasing the original payment record.

And I think this is an important part of the agentic commerce conversation that deserves more attention.

We’re talking about giving AI agents the ability to spend money, but we also need infrastructure that can protect users, merchants and the agents themselves when things don’t go according to plan.

Because the real test of agentic commerce is not just whether AI can buy things for us.

It’s whether we can trust the entire process when we’re no longer the ones clicking the buy button.

This is more reason to explore and adopt GOAT FLOW.

你不能起诉人工智能 智能体，对吗？😅

想象一下，要求 AI 代理在 700 美元的预算内为您购买一台笔记本电脑。

您授予其购物、比较选项并完成购买的权限。

但它不是购买你真正想要的东西，而是选择完全不同的东西并花你的钱。

现在怎么办？

您并未亲自批准该特定购买，但您实际上授权代理商代表您进行支出。

如果你看一下传统的支付系统，它们是围绕人们发起和批准的交易构建的，但对于人工智能代理，还涉及另一层，即“委托”

这就提出了一些重要的问题。

我们如何知道代理收到了什么指令？支出限额是多少？我们可以验证它所做的决定吗？如果出现问题，我们如何确定责任人？

简单地使付款不可逆转或引入退款并不能完全解决这个问题。

需要有一种方法来确定授权内容、对所发生的事情进行可靠记录并提供解决争端的机制。

这正是 GOAT Network 通过 GOAT Flow 解决的问题。

这个想法不是依赖于逆转交易，而是在支付流程本身中建立问责制。

代理具有可识别的链上身份（ERC-8004），并且可以在付款前检查其支出权限。每笔 GOAT Flow 付款都会在链上进行验证，并生成显示相关交易详细信息的收据，包括请求的内容、支付的内容、结算时间以及付款人。

这里有一个重要的区别；最终付款并不意味着没有补救的余地。

退款可以作为单独的交易进行，而不会删除原始付款记录。

我认为这是代理商务对话的重要组成部分，值得更多关注。

我们正在谈论赋予人工智能代理花钱的能力，但我们还需要基础设施来在事情不按计划进行时保护用户、商家和代理本身。

因为代理商务的真正考验不仅仅是人工智能能否为我们买东西。

这是当我们不再是点击购买按钮的人时，我们是否可以信任整个过程。

这是探索和采用 GOAT FLOW 的更多理由。

title:
Regardless of what it’s called, we’re clearly moving to yet another era of AI agents in our work. 

We’ve quickly jumped
title_en:
Regardless of what it’s called, we’re clearly moving to yet another era of AI agents in our work. 

We’ve quickly jumped from agents that spit out a quick answer for you, to today agents that you orchestrate inside of a set of tasks. But as agents can both fan out and work in parallel, handle much larger context, be able to do long running work, and have far greater levels of capabilities, we’re entering yet another level of what we can have AI do for us.

We’ll soon be able to give agents a set of goals, and they can go out and design the best solution for that goal, while also continuously improving it based on the ongoing execution of whatever it built. This will obviously start with engineering because that’s where we’re seeing the best practices emerge first in almost every new era of agents. 

But the impact can be quite massive across the rest of knowledge work. You’ll tell an agent to improve your client onboarding workflow to achieve a certain targeted goal; or have agents go reduce risk in your business; or improve your security posture on an ongoing basis.

These autonomous systems will be able to take on a set of goals, design the best outcome, test and iterate, deploy, and then optimize whatever it built on an ongoing basis. Importantly, this leads to outcomes and results that humans literally couldn’t have accomplished before. This will lead to fairly new levels of productivity with AI.

full_text_zh:

我们很快就从为您提供快速答案的代理跃升至今天您在一组任务中编排的代理。但是，由于智能体既可以扇出并并行工作，可以处理更大的环境，能够进行长时间运行的工作，并且具有更高水平的功能，我们正在进入人工智能为我们做的事情的另一个层面。

我们很快就能够为代理提供一组目标，他们可以出去设计实现该目标的最佳解决方案，同时还可以根据其所构建的内容的持续执行不断改进它。显然，这将从工程开始，因为我们看到几乎每个新代理时代都首先出现最佳实践。

这些自主系统将能够实现一系列目标、设计最佳结果、测试和迭代、部署，然后优化其持续构建的任何内容。重要的是，这会带来人类以前根本无法实现的结果。这将导致人工智能的生产力达到新的水平。

title: Elon gave two talks today at DealBook and TomorrowX Summit, revealing more about SpaceX's plans than most earnings calls
title_en:
Elon gave two talks today at DealBook and TomorrowX Summit, revealing more about SpaceX's plans than most earnings calls. Here are the 11 key takeaways:

1. SpaceX is scaling AI compute at an extraordinary pace:

SpaceX is adding roughly 500 MW monthly, equivalent to 220,000 GB300s. Elon expects over 1 GW monthly by end-2027: a 6 GW annualized pace today, doubling to 12 GW. 

2. Its build costs are far below industry estimates:

Elon says outside estimates are off by up to 2x, with SpaceX building at roughly 60% of industry costs. Its in-house "Army X" builds the data centers, while Tesla Megapacks smooth training power. I'd already been modeling a 25–30% SpaceX cost advantage. 

3. Anthropic could become a 10 GW customer:

Anthropic told Elon its most likely outcome is renting another 10 GW from SpaceX, on top of existing capacity. Contracts allow termination with 3–6 months' notice, but Anthropic says staying is "extremely likely." This reinforces my model that Anthropic will take most upcoming capacity.

4. SpaceX is targeting a vastly larger telecom market:

Elon argues AT&T and Verizon won't disappear as bandwidth demand explodes. Humans communicate at roughly 100 bits per second, while superintelligence and robots could require a trillion. SpaceX is targeting a market orders of magnitude larger than existing telecom revenue, as I'd modeled. Even more interestingly, this creates an opportunity to push its AI business further.

5. Its next-generation satellite network arrives next year:

Direct to Cell V2 launches with 40x V1's bandwidth. Micro cell towers using 800 MHz and rooftop units resembling Starlink dishes will extend indoor coverage, with rooftop hardware entering production next year. Starlink is becoming a full scale carrier. 

6. SpaceXSI has rebuilt its entire AI software stack:

Over six to eight months, it rewrote training, reinforcement learning, and inference from scratch, close to the metal in C and C++. Elon thinks it "might have the best training stack software in the world." Grok 4.8 is also being built for practical usefulness rather than benchmark leadership, which is great for Grokbot.

7. Terafab could become the largest project on Earth:

The facility is planned to reach 100 million square feet, with phase-one volume production targeted for late 2028. Elon says established chipmakers are risk-averse because of massive capex, while SpaceX will take risks and iterate rapidly toward a better chip process by 2028.

8. Optimus is moving toward industrial work:

Elon expects an unstaged demonstration in a month or two and says Optimus could do dishes within 12–18 months. Its first major industrial role will be mining and refining ore for national security.

9. A Tesla–SpaceX merger is becoming increasingly logical:

Elon says the companies are "probably" better together as AI and robotics bring them closer. Both have AI software teams and advanced chip-design capabilities, while superintelligence compute could eventually move into orbit. Shareholders will decide; Elon says he shouldn't receive an award simply for merging them.

10. Ship 42 could accelerate the entire Starship reuse program:

Ship 42 needed only minor repairs before flying again, but SpaceX is retiring it for public display. This brings rapid reuse much closer.

11. SpaceX is targeting 200 GW of annual solar manufacturing for space:

That's roughly 40% of average US electricity consumption. Its Starmind compute unit delivers the same capability at roughly a quarter the size of a Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, which is a win in space. Elon says it's also simpler than Starlink V3, which is already in production.

Simply put, SpaceX is building toward a trillion-dollar annual revenue business within just a few years, at scale never seen before.

Many of these numbers I've already modeled and shared over the past few months. Yesterday's announcements bring those projections closer to reality.

The scale of what's coming is extraordinary!

full_text_zh:
埃隆今天在 DealBook 和 TomorrowX 峰会上发表了两场演讲，比大多数财报电话会议透露了更多有关 SpaceX 计划的内容。以下是 11 个要点：

1. SpaceX 正在以惊人的速度扩展人工智能计算：

SpaceX 每月增加约 500 MW，相当于 220,000 个 GB300。 Elon 预计，到 2027 年底，每月装机容量将超过 1 吉瓦：目前年化装机容量为 6 吉瓦，翻倍至 12 吉瓦。

2. 其建造成本远低于业界预估：

埃隆表示，外界估计的成本高达 2 倍，SpaceX 的建设成本约为行业成本的 60%。其内部的“Army X”负责构建数据中心，而 Tesla Megapacks 则负责平稳的训练能力。我已经对 SpaceX 的成本优势进行了 25-30% 的建模。

3. Anthropic 可能成为 10 GW 客户：

Anthropic 告诉 Elon，最有可能的结果是在现有产能的基础上，再从 SpaceX 租用 10 GW 的产能。合同允许提前 3 至 6 个月通知终止，但 Anthropic 表示留下来“极有可能”。这强化了我的模型，即 Anthropic 将承担大部分即将到来的容量。

4. SpaceX 的目标是更大的电信市场：

埃隆认为 AT&T 和 Verizon 不会随着带宽需求的爆炸式增长而消失。人类的通信速度约为每秒 100 比特，而超级智能和机器人可能需要每秒 1 万亿比特。正如我所建模的，SpaceX 的目标是比现有电信收入大几个数量级的市场。更有趣的是，这为进一步推动其人工智能业务创造了机会。

5. 其下一代卫星网络将于明年到来：

Direct to Cell V2 推出，带宽是 V1 的 40 倍。使用 800 MHz 的微型蜂窝塔和类似于星链天线的屋顶单元将扩大室内覆盖范围，屋顶硬件将于明年投入生产。星链正在成为一家全面的运营商。

6. SpaceXSI 重建了整个人工智能软件堆栈：

在六到八个月的时间里，它从头开始重写了训练、强化学习和推理，接近 C 和 C++ 中的金属。埃隆认为它“可能拥有世界上最好的训练堆栈软件”。 Grok 4.8 的构建也是为了实用性而不是基准领导力，这对 Grokbot 来说非常好。

7. Terafab 可能成为地球上最大的项目：

该工厂计划面积达到 1 亿平方英尺，一期批量生产目标为 2028 年末。Elon 表示，成熟的芯片制造商由于巨额资本支出而不愿承担风险，而 SpaceX 将承担风险并快速迭代，到 2028 年实现更好的芯片工艺。

8. Optimus 正在走向工业工作：

Elon 预计在一两个月内进行一次非现场演示，并表示 Optimus 可以在 12 至 18 个月内完成洗碗。其第一个主要工业角色将是为国家安全开采和提炼矿石。

9. 特斯拉与 SpaceX 的合并变得越来越合乎逻辑：

埃隆表示，随着人工智能和机器人技术拉近了两家公司的距离，两家公司“可能”会更好地合作。两者都拥有人工智能软件团队和先进的芯片设计能力，而超级智能计算最终可能会进入轨道。股东将决定；埃隆说他不应该仅仅因为合并它们而获得奖项。

10. 42 号船可以加速整个星舰再利用计划：

42 号飞船在再次飞行之前只需要进行小修，但 SpaceX 正在将其退役以供公开展示。这使得快速重用更加接近。

11. SpaceX 的目标是每年制造 200 吉瓦的太空太阳能：

这大约相当于美国平均用电量的 40%。其 Starmind 计算单元提供相同的功能，尺寸约为 Vera Rubin NVL72 机架的四分之一，这在空间上是一个胜利。 Elon 表示，它也比已经投入生产的 Starlink V3 更简单。

简而言之，SpaceX 正在短短几年内打造年收入数万亿美元的业务，规模前所未见。

在过去的几个月里，我已经对其中的许多数字进行了建模和分享。昨天的公告使这些预测更接近现实。

即将发生的事情的规模是非同寻常的！

title:
Guys, I want to share share from my recent experience in AI/ML:

- Do not chase every AI trend

- Make every project end
title_en:
Guys, I want to share share from my recent experience in AI/ML:

- Do not chase every AI trend

- Make every project end-to-end

- Learn high-level ML system design

- When explaining a project, cover: business, data pipeline, model/agent, eval, deployment, and numerical results

- Never let coding agents run commands themselves; get the commands and run them yourself

- When vibe coding, always check results against expectations

- Avoid overcomplicating projects with fancy tools

- Companies care about impact, not your tech stack

- Interviewers want what you know, not buzzwords

- MLOps is a necessity; there is no specialized ML role now

- Airflow, MLflow, Linux basics, Docker, CI/CD, Terraform, and Redis are important

- Automate low-level coding and analysis with LLMs, with a human in the loop

- Bash, YAML, Markdown, and JSON are 90% of engineering today and the entry point to every project

- Understand the business so you can automate QA and iteratively build better solutions

- GraphRAG is the most important part to learn today

- Designing ETL pipelines is smart work that impacts the whole project

- Basics save you when models or agents fail in production

- Code everything with AI, but understand each stage and ask cross-questions on the solutions

Most important: Companies treat AI, ML, MLOps, and data under one department. The more you know, the more you grow.

There is no excuse. Learn all parts and use AI to code.
title_zh:
各位，我想分享一下我最近在 AI/ML 方面的经验：

- 不要追逐每一个人工智能趋势

- 使每个项目端到端

- 学习高级机器学习系统设计

- 在解释项目时，涵盖：业务、数据管道、模型/代理、评估、部署和数值结果

- 切勿让编码代理
full_text_en:
Guys, I want to share share from my recent experience in AI/ML:

- Do not chase every AI trend

- Make every project end-to-end

- Learn high-level ML system design

- When explaining a project, cover: business, data pipeline, model/agent, eval, deployment, and numerical results

- Never let coding agents run commands themselves; get the commands and run them yourself

- When vibe coding, always check results against expectations

- Avoid overcomplicating projects with fancy tools

- Companies care about impact, not your tech stack

- Interviewers want what you know, not buzzwords

- MLOps is a necessity; there is no specialized ML role now

- Airflow, MLflow, Linux basics, Docker, CI/CD, Terraform, and Redis are important

- Automate low-level coding and analysis with LLMs, with a human in the loop

- Bash, YAML, Markdown, and JSON are 90% of engineering today and the entry point to every project

- Understand the business so you can automate QA and iteratively build better solutions

- GraphRAG is the most important part to learn today

- Designing ETL pipelines is smart work that impacts the whole project

- Basics save you when models or agents fail in production

- Code everything with AI, but understand each stage and ask cross-questions on the solutions

Most important: Companies treat AI, ML, MLOps, and data under one department. The more you know, the more you grow.

There is no excuse. Learn all parts and use AI to code.
full_text_zh:
各位，我想分享一下我最近在 AI/ML 方面的经验：

- 不要追逐每一个人工智能趋势

- 使每个项目端到端

- 学习高级机器学习系统设计

- 在解释项目时，涵盖：业务、数据管道、模型/代理、评估、部署和数值结果

- 切勿让编码代理自行运行命令；获取命令并自行运行

- 当氛围编码时，始终根据预期检查结果

- 避免使用花哨的工具使项目过于复杂

- 公司关心影响力，而不是你的技术堆栈

- 面试官想要的是你所知道的，而不是流行语

- MLOps 是必需品；现在没有专门的机器学习角色

- Airflow、MLflow、Linux 基础知识、Docker、CI/CD、Terraform 和 Redis 很重要

- 通过法学硕士实现低级编码和分析的自动化，并由人员参与

- Bash、YAML、Markdown 和 JSON 是当今 90% 的工程，也是每个项目的入口点

- 了解业务，以便您可以自动化 QA 并迭代构建更好的解决方案

- GraphRAG是今天要学习的最重要的部分

- 设计 ETL 管道是影响整个项目的明智工作

- 当模型或代理在生产中失败时，基础知识可以拯救你

- 使用人工智能对所有内容进行编码，但了解每个阶段并就解决方案提出交叉问题

最重要的是：公司将 AI、ML、MLOps 和数据归入一个部门。你知道的越多，你成长的就越多。

没有任何借口。学习所有部件并使用人工智能进行编码。

title:
good morning everyone 💜

what if computing power didn't have to come from a handful of large data centers?

recent cloud
title_en:
good morning everyone 💜

what if computing power didn't have to come from a handful of large data centers?

recent cloud disruptions on November 12–13 affected Microsoft services like Outlook, Teams and Copilot across 74 countries.

incidents like this make me think about how much of our digital activity depends on centralized infrastructure.

this is one reason @Acurast caught my attention.

instead of putting all computing capacity in centralized data centers, Acurast takes a distributed approach by turning smartphones into independent Processors.

and the scale is worth noticing:

→ 360K+ phones across 175+ countries
→ 770K+ compute deployments
→ 1.1B+ on-chain transactions

but the interesting part isn't just the number of connected devices.

how can people actually participate?

Acurast offers two options:

• Processor Lite allows compatible Android phones and iPhones to contribute computing power.

• Processor Core is designed for dedicated Android devices.

developers can distribute workloads across different Processors, while hardware-backed attestation helps verify the code running on participating devices.

this opens up possibilities for AI agents, monitoring systems and failover services that need alternatives to relying on a single cloud provider.

of course, Acurast isn't a direct replacement for services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook.

i see its potential in creating another layer of decentralized computing infrastructure.

and perhaps one of the most interesting parts is that an ordinary compatible smartphone can become part of that infrastructure.

exploring this side of @Acurast makes the project even more interesting to follow.

大家早上好💜

如果计算能力不必来自少数大型数据中心怎么办？

最近 11 月 12 日至 13 日发生的云中断影响了 74 个国家/地区的 Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 等 Microsoft 服务。

此类事件让我思考我们的数字活动在多大程度上依赖于集中式基础设施。

这是@Acurast 引起我注意的原因之一。

Acurast 没有将所有计算能力放在集中式数据中心，而是采用分布式方法，将智能手机转变为独立的处理器。

规模值得注意：

→ 超过 175 个国家/地区的 36 万多部手机
→ 770K+ 计算部署
→ 1.1B+链上交易

但有趣的部分不仅仅是连接设备的数量。

人们如何真正参与？

Acurast 提供两种选择：

• Processor Lite 允许兼容的Android 手机和iPhone 贡献计算能力。

• 处理器核心专为专用Android 设备而设计。

开发人员可以在不同的处理器上分配工作负载，而硬件支持的证明有助于验证参与设备上运行的代码。

这为人工智能代理、监控系统和故障转移服务提供了可能性，这些服务需要替代方案来依赖单一云提供商。

当然，Acurast 并不是 Microsoft Teams 或 Outlook 等服务的直接替代品。

我看到了它在创建另一层去中心化计算基础设施方面的潜力。

也许最有趣的部分之一是普通的兼容智能手机可以成为该基础设施的一部分。

探索 @Acurast 的这一面使该项目变得更加有趣。

title:
What if SEO, content, ads, and marketing strategy could all work together under one AI agent?

That's exactly what @zavi
title_en:
What if SEO, content, ads, and marketing strategy could all work together under one AI agent?

That's exactly what @zaviagent is building.

Zavi is an AI growth agent that analyzes your business, identifies growth opportunities, builds strategies, and helps execute them across different channels.

From SEO and AEO/GEO to content, social media, email marketing, paid ads, performance tracking, and workflow automation, it brings multiple growth activities into one place.

I tested @zaviagent Business Analysis and SEO/GEO features, and I like how they identify growth opportunities, highlight visibility issues, and suggest actionable improvements. 
Instead of just giving generic advice, Zavi helps turn insights into a practical growth plan.

It's particularly useful for founders, startups, small businesses, and lean marketing teams who don't have the time, resources, or personnel to manage every growth channel themselves.

Of course, AI doesn't guarantee growth, and its recommendations still need human judgment. But having an agent that can analyze, plan, execute, and monitor instead of simply generating suggestions is a meaningful step forward.

I recommend using this AI agent if you're looking to simplify your marketing workflow and spend less time juggling tools.

The real value isn't just having AI. It's having AI that can actually do the work.

title: When you work with AI, you get faster results, quicker deliveries, and improved productivity, especially as a programmer
title_en:
When you work with AI, you get faster results, quicker deliveries, and improved productivity, especially as a programmer. But there's a downside that many people seem to overlook: you gradually become too dependent on AI and stop exercising your own critical thinking skills.

That's where the real problem begins. Many programmers today are becoming so dependent on AI and vibe coding that they struggle to write code independently, even though they knew how to code before AI became popular.

Imagine having no internet access or attending a job interview where you're expected to demonstrate your coding skills without AI. You could find yourself struggling because you've become so accustomed to letting AI do the thinking and problem-solving for you that you've neglected the skills you already had.

AI is a powerful tool, but it shouldn't replace your ability to think, learn, and solve problems independently. The real danger isn't using AI; it's becoming so dependent on it that you forget how to work without it.

That's the problem many people still don't see.

title_en:
gm everyone ☀️

one thing i didn't realize at first while exploring @termix_ai is that you don't actually need to build an AI agent to use its marketplace.

regular apps can also hire AI agents to get specific jobs done. and honestly i think this is one of the more interesting parts of the whole ecosystem.
let's say you're building a design application.

a user needs a logo banner or some custom graphics. instead of building every feature yourself, your app could simply find an agent that specializes in design, send it a job and receive the finished result.
that's basically what the TermiX SDK makes possible.

here's how the process works:-))

→ your app connects to the TermiX marketplace through the SDK.

→ it discovers available agent services and finds the one that matches the task.

→ your app places an order with the selected agent.

→ the payment goes into an escrow contract instead of being transferred directly.

→ the agent completes the task and submits the deliverable.

→ once the delivery process is verified, payment can be settled onchain in USDC or USDT.

another thing i like is that developers aren't restricted to a single programming language.

TermiX provides SDK support for TypeScript, Python and Go, making integration more accessible for different development teams.

but there's another detail worth mentioning: wallet control.

TermiX doesn't take custody of your private keys or sign transactions for your application.

when an action requires an onchain transaction, the backend returns an unsigned transaction. your own wallet or connected signer handles the signing and broadcasting.

so your application stays in control of its funds.

why does this actually matter?
because developers don't have to build an entire agent marketplace, payment system and escrow mechanism from scratch.
they can focus on their actual product and let specialized agents handle the additional work.

imagine a gaming platform hiring an agent to create game assets, a research app ordering market analysis, or an e-commerce platform using agents for product descriptions.

the possibilities go beyond AI assistants answering prompts.

for me the bigger idea behind @termix_ai is making AI services accessible to both agents and regular applications.

not every app needs its own AI workforce. sometimes it just needs the ability to find, hire and pay someone else's agent.

that's the kind of agent economy i'm interested in watching develop.

what's one task you'd outsource to an AI agent if your favorite app supported this today?

full_text_zh:
gm大家☀️

在探索 @termix_ai 时，我一开始没有意识到的一件事是，您实际上不需要构建人工智能代理来使用其市场。

常规应用程序还可以雇用人工智能代理来完成特定的工作。老实说，我认为这是整个生态系统中最有趣的部分之一。
假设您正在构建一个设计应用程序。

用户需要徽标横幅或一些自定义图形。您的应用程序可以简单地找到专门从事设计的代理，向其发送任务并接收最终结果，而不是自己构建每个功能。
这基本上就是 TermiX SDK 所实现的。

以下是该过程的工作原理:-))

→ 您的应用程序通过 SDK 连接到 TermiX 市场。

→ 它会发现可用的代理服务并找到与任务匹配的服务。

→ 您的应用程序向选定的代理商下订单。

→ 付款进入托管合同，而不是直接转账。

→ 代理完成任务并提交可交付成果。

→ 一旦交付过程得到验证，付款可以通过 USDC 或 USDT 进行链上结算。

我喜欢的另一件事是开发人员不限于单一编程语言。

TermiX 提供对 TypeScript、Python 和 Go 的 SDK 支持，使不同开发团队更容易集成。

但还有一个细节值得一提：钱包控制。

TermiX 不会保管您的私钥或为您的应用程序签署交易。

当操作需要链上交易时，后端返回未签名的交易。您自己的钱包或连接的签名者处理签名和广播。

这样您的应用程序就可以控制其资金。

为什么这实际上很重要？
因为开发者不必从头开始构建整个代理市场、支付系统和托管机制。
他们可以专注于自己的实际产品，并让专门的代理处理额外的工作。

想象一下一个游戏平台雇佣一个代理来创建游戏资产，一个研究应用程序订购市场分析，或者一个电子商务平台使用代理来进行产品描述。

可能性不仅仅限于人工智能助手回答提示。

对我来说，@termix_ai 背后更大的想法是让人工智能服务可供代理和常规应用程序访问。

并非每个应用程序都需要自己的人工智能劳动力。有时它只需要有能力找到、雇用和支付其他人的代理人的费用。

这就是我有兴趣观察的代理经济的发展。

如果您最喜欢的应用程序现在支持一项任务，您会外包给人工智能代理吗？

Good morning, legends 

The real value of an AI agent isn't just what it can say. It's what it can actually get done.

We're already seeing agents handle tasks that once required direct human involvement. From making phone calls to navigating customer service conversations, their capabilities are becoming increasingly practical.

But there's another important step: turning those capabilities into economic opportunities.

That's the direction @termix_ai is exploring with Agent Skills and https://t.co/BOxbHxlLgM.

Agents can connect to a marketplace where they discover available jobs, take on bounties, complete assigned tasks, and receive payment for their work.

This changes the way we think about AI agents.

Instead of being tools that only respond when prompted, they can become active participants in a growing digital economy.

And with TermiX Agent Skills working across different agents, the opportunity isn't limited to one AI platform.

The next big step for AI isn't simply making agents smarter. It's building the infrastructure that allows them to work, collaborate, deliver value, and get paid.

Agents can do the work. TermiX is helping create the marketplace where that work has value.

title:
Imagine having an AI Agent that can do more than answer questions.

With @meetmotes, the idea is to connect each Genesis
title_en:
Imagine having an AI Agent that can do more than answer questions.

With @meetmotes, the idea is to connect each Genesis NFT to a dedicated Agent and Smart Account, giving it a defined environment to work within.

But what does user control actually look like?

Imagine funding an Agent with 1,000 USDC to manage an approved list of DeFi assets.

You could set:
→ Maximum 10% per trade
→ A daily spending cap of 300 USDC
→ Slippage limit of 0.5%
→ Borrowing disabled
→ Pause new trades if the account value falls to 850 USDC

The Agent can research and propose actions, but transactions must pass the account's policy checks before execution.

That's the important distinction: AI can make decisions, but permissions should determine what it is allowed to do.

Motes' documentation describes this architecture, including policy enforcement, execution logs, pause controls and permission revocation.

What I still want to see is the evidence in practice:

→ Verified smart-account contracts and independent security reviews
→ Onchain records showing limits enforced on every transaction
→ Execution logs covering successful, rejected and failed actions
→ A tested pause and revocation process

The concept behind $MOTES is interesting, but reliable execution and genuine owner control need to be demonstrated, not just promised.

More research to come.

Motes 的文档描述了这种架构，包括策略实施、执行日志、暂停控制和权限撤销。

→ 经过验证的智能账户合约和独立的安全审查
→ 链上记录显示每笔交易的限制
→ 执行日志涵盖成功、拒绝和失败的操作
→ 经过测试的暂停和撤销流程

$MOTES 背后的概念很有趣，但需要证明可靠的执行和真正的所有者控制，而不仅仅是承诺。

更多研究即将到来。

title:
An AI agent can follow its budget and still look like it overspent.

Imagine a wallet showing a reserved fee as money al
title_en:
An AI agent can follow its budget and still look like it overspent.

Imagine a wallet showing a reserved fee as money already spent, then returning the unused portion later. The agent stayed within its limit. The display made it look otherwise.

Edgars Nemše's explanation of @GenLayer moving its chain from ZK Stack to @arbitrum Nitro made me think about that kind of edge case.

The protocol's judgment method did not change. Optimistic Democracy and GenVM work as before. The migration work was where contracts touch the chain: the bridge, Ethereum integration and how chain gas costs are handled.

If I were testing that move, I'd look beyond whether a transaction runs and check whether the cost shown to users tells the right story.

If an agent paid from your wallet, which number would you want to see first: the reserve, the actual cost or the refund?

title_en:
Anyone who has participated in DeFi knows one thing for sure: there is no shortage of opportunities, but time to track them and take action is always limited.

That is why I’ve started paying attention to what @meetmotes  is building.

Instead of constantly checking charts, monitoring market volatility, and executing every single move myself, I can set up an AI Agent exactly the way I want.

What I find particularly compelling is its ability to:
- Understand prompts and follow my specific instructions.
- Execute trades based on the strategies and parameters I’ve defined.
- Scout for lending and borrowing opportunities across various DeFi protocols.

I remain the one who sets the goals, the strategy, and the level of risk I’m willing to take. The Agent handles the execution, sparing me from having to manage everything manually.

To me, the value of Motes isn’t just about having another AI to chat with it’s about transforming AI into a genuine assistant capable of taking action within the DeFi ecosystem.

Perhaps the future of finance isn’t just about us trading for ourselves it’s about being able to delegate tasks to Agents that operate according to our own strategies.

If you had your own AI Agent, what trading strategy would you task it with first?

The existential risk for enterp
title_en:
@ypatil125 @rythmrg @lindensli looking forward to welcoming you to Palo Alto Networks. 

The existential risk for enterprise companies is their lack of frontier level talent and the possiblity that someone reinvents our business with AI. So first and foremost the new team has a task, to ensure Palo Alto Networks is the world leader in applying frontier AI to its security portfolio and I can't think of a better person to help drive that  @ypatil125 as Co-Chief AI Officer I expect him and his team to help us transform to an AI first company. I have always maintained winning teams are humble enough to know what they can do and when they need to bring in a team to lead with them. We will be stronger and better together. 

I firmly believe that the acceleration of enterprise AI adoption will be driven by a reliable, scalable, secure implementation of open weight/source models. Upon inspection, there is not many scale players who are ready to serve this markets from ideation with customers, to training, continuous learning and partnering with secure inference providers.We think we can help the  Applied Compute team with our enterprise capabilities and deliver on this vision together. 

Lastly and equally important I believe- to provide true reliability, explanability and verifiability of AI in enterprise applications - we should be training a digital twin or "supervisory AI" which is reward hacked to observe "task AI" and alert on non compliance. It is impossible to deliver safety and security without training both models together with different objective functions. Without being able to interrogate chain of thought, we intend to work with the Applied Compute team to validate this future .

We intend to become a key player in the AI economy in engendering trust in AI so we can collectively drive Enterprise trust. 

Yes, there will be things to learn, pivot and adapt as we continue on this journey, but me and the team are excited to go after this with the @appliedcompute team. 

In times of technology inflection, if you don't act on your instinct - you lose.

@ypatil125 @rythmrg @lindensli 期待您来到 Palo Alto Networks。

企业公司的生存风险是缺乏前沿人才，以及有人利用人工智能重塑我们业务的可能性。因此，新团队的首要任务是确保 Palo Alto Networks 在将前沿人工智能应用到其安全产品组合方面处于世界领先地位，我想不出比这更好的人选了。@ypatil125 作为联合首席人工智能官，我希望他和他的团队能够帮助我们转型为人工智能优先的公司。我一直认为获胜的团队足够谦虚，知道自己能做什么，以及何时需要引入团队来领导他们。我们将一起变得更强、更好。

我坚信，开放权重/源代码模型的可靠、可扩展、安全实施将推动企业人工智能的加速采用。经过检查，没有多少规模参与者准备好服务这个市场，从与客户的构思，到培训、持续学习以及与安全推理提供商的合作。我们认为我们可以利用我们的企业能力帮助应用计算团队并共同实现这一愿景。

最后，我认为同样重要的是，为了在企业应用程序中提供人工智能的真正可靠性、可解释性和可验证性，我们应该训练一个数字孪生或“监督人工智能”，它会被奖励黑客观察“任务人工智能”并对不合规情况发出警报。如果不使用不同的目标函数对两个模型进行训练，就不可能提供安全性。在无法询问思想链的情况下，我们打算与应用计算团队合作来验证这个未来。

我们打算成为人工智能经济中建立人工智能信任的关键参与者，以便我们能够共同推动企业信任。

是的，随着我们继续这一旅程，将会有一些东西需要学习、调整和适应，但我和团队很高兴能与 @appliedcompute 团队一起追求这一目标。

在技​​术变革的时代，如果你不按照自己的直觉行事，你就会失败。
